subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land the bounded provider-normalized tool-schema parameter cache now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The source-visible repeated-normalization path is clear, but the permanent cache lifecycle affects provider hook ownership, plugin metadata, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime rollout.

options.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated hot-path work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live provider proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini or heap proof confirms that the user-visible impact still occurs on a real provider path.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr owns the adjacent prepared-runtime migration tracker and is the best available owner for deciding cache-vs-prepared-runtime boundaries.
